newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson seen buying Miller stake in brewery.
newsitem.headline: Molson seen buying Miller stake in brewery.

text.p: Molson Cos Ltd could be considering buying back a 20 percent stake in Molson Breweries it had previously sold in a bid to return to its brewing roots.

Analysts speculated on Thursday that Molson Cos chairman Eric Molson would try to buy back the 20 percent stake from Miller Brewing Co rather than seek Miller's approval for a proposed partnership with arch rival Adolf Coors Co to manage Coors products in Canada.

"Eric has figured out that his heritage is in the beer industry and I think they would like to buy the block back if they can get it at a reasonable price," Michael Palmer, analyst for Loewen Ondaatje McCutcheon.
Molson Cos, which owns 40 percent of Molson Breweries, has about C$650 million in cash, analysts said. They estimated it would cost between C$200 million and C$300 million to buy Miller's stake.
Molson Cos spokesman Brian Crombie declined to comment on the possibility of a buyout. But he said Molson would have to offer half of any buyout to its other partner Foster's Brewing Group Ltd.

"There is a stipulation in the partnership agreement that any partner buying another partner's interest has to offer that partner's interest on a pro rata basis to the other partner. So if we bought Miller's stake we would have to offer half of it to Foster's," Crombie said.
Molson Breweries is also owned 40 percent by Foster's Brewing Group.
Molson has been looking for a brewing acquisition since it sold off most of its non-beer assets last year.
Miller spokesman Michael Brophy declined to comment on the speculation about Miller's stake in Molson.
Research Capital Corp analyst Jacques Kavafian said that a recent press release from Miller parent Philip Morris Co may provide a clue to Miller's intentions.
"(Wednesday's) press release from Philip Morris mentioned that Miller is focusing on its core brands and they named the core brands, none of which were Molson brands," Kavafian said.
"That's a signal that they are going to get rid of Molson," Kavafian said.
Molson said on Wednesday that it had settled a dispute with Adolph Coors in their battle over Molson's licensing rights to Coors' top-selling beers in Canada.
Under the agreement, Molson paid Coors C$100 million and also agreed to form a new partnership with Coors and Foster's Brewing to manage Coors brands in Canada.
The proposed partnership will be owned 50.1 percent by Coors and 24.95 percent each by Molson and Foster's.
The partnership and brewing agreement is subject to regulatory approval and approval from Miller Brewing before December 31, 1997.
Pending Miller's approval, Molson Breweries and Coors have agreed that Molson Breweries will continue to brew and market Coors product for an interim period through December 31, 1997.
If Miller does not give its approval, all Molson Breweries' arrangements with Coors will terminate no later than June 15, 1998, the statement said.
Last October, an arbitration panel tore up Molson's contract for Coors Light and Original Coors, which accounted for eight percent of the Canadian brewer's sales volume.
The panel said Molson breached its licensing deal by allowing Miller Brewing Co to buy a 20 percent stake in the Canadian brewer in 1993 without Coors consent.
